QUALITY AND COORDINATION

Design Review, Independent Review and Approval: Use the Terms Precisely

Clear language prevents an intended review from becoming an unsupported credential.

In this insight

Define each step in the project processDistinguish planned from completed workClarify what the review coversKeep responsibility visibleFor your project discussionDiscuss a project ↗

Educational overview · Project-specific design and execution require qualified review.

Define each step in the project process

Design preparation, checking, independent review and approval may involve different parties and different scopes. Ask the project team to describe the actual arrangement rather than rely on a broad phrase such as fully vetted. The contract and relevant requirements should establish what each step means. Precise language helps the client understand which decisions have been made and which remain outstanding.

Distinguish planned from completed work

A proposal may state that a review will be undertaken by a specified institution or equivalent body. That is a future commitment, not evidence that the current design has already been reviewed or endorsed. Keep the status explicit in project documents and public descriptions. Request the relevant record when the review occurs and understand any conditions or limitations attached to it.

Clarify what the review covers

A review may address a defined design package rather than the entire project or construction operation. Identify the documents, revisions and scope involved. If the design changes, ask whether further review is required. Avoid extending a review statement beyond its documented basis, particularly when communicating capability to stakeholders who were not involved in the technical process.

Keep responsibility visible

Review does not automatically erase the responsibilities of the originating designer, contractor or client. The project team should understand the contractual and professional allocation. Maintain the review trail with the approved information set and track outstanding comments to closure. Accurate terminology supports confidence because it tells stakeholders exactly what evidence exists instead of asking them to rely on a broad assurance.

For your project discussion

Use these questions to structure a conversation with the project’s qualified design and delivery team. This article is general procurement guidance, not a site-specific design, method statement or compliance assessment. The cited international resources provide background; applicable local requirements and the approved project documents govern the work.

Take this into your next conversation

  • Define the actual review stages.
  • Separate planned review from completed evidence.
  • State the scope and revision covered.

References & further reading

  • Further reading: FHWA — Construction inspection checklists

International references provide technical context; applicable local requirements and the project engineer’s decisions govern the actual works.
